General State reaction to Proposed Legislation
Arizona--While comments are generally constructive, they tend to reject
the statement because the proposed legislation would provide authority for
the Federal Government to regulate the taking of resident endangered species.
Florida--No comments adverse to the statement. Comment included private groups which were outspoken in their endorsement of the proposed legislation.
Indiana--"State cannot endorse the legislation as currently proposed"
because of strong objections by the Department of Natural Resources.
<u>Iowa--</u>Only the Department of Health responded to the Clearinghouse, and their reply was no comment at this time.
Kansas--While the Parks and Resources Authority finds the statement contributes to the State Recreation Plan and does not conflict with any activities of the Authority, the Forestry, Fish and Game Commission believes the proposed legislation will accomplish little for endangered species. They also object to transfer of resident wildlife jurisdiction from State to Federal agencies.
Kentucky--Comment is generally favorable. The Program Development Office notes with satisfaction the provisions for a "likely to become threatened" list, Federal and State coordination, and removal of the land acquisition ceiling. The Department of Fish and Wildlife Resources comments constructively on several points without endorsement or rejection of the proposal.
Maine--Neither supports nor rejects the statement but protests a change in the law that would deprive the States of their "strong role in the management of rare and endangered species within its jurisdiction."
Maryland -- "Concurs with the intent of the proposed legislation."
